checkedAgainst: the plain-writing and short-screen rules (Dan, 20 and 21 Oct)
safety: never show an unsafe step

faults.finding: 'Once the rotor is turning, though, the same winding keeps it going' is stated with no why. It is the step behind the 'not momentum' trap and the 'runs if spun' fault.
faults.fix: Add one 'One way to picture it' line: a pulsing field acts like two equal fields turning opposite ways; at rest they pull equally, once the rotor turns one way the field turning with it pulls harder.

faults.where: screen 3, first wrong option and its hint
faults.finding: 'To keep its current low, so it runs cool' is half true in the example (6.00 A against 9.82 A), and the hint's 'thin wire runs hotter' is loose: it is the current density that heats it fast.
faults.fix: Make the slip 'So it can stay in and help the motor run' (the start winding left in), with a hint on its high current density and the switch.

faults.finding: 'Swapping the supply leads changes nothing' is wider than the point: it changes nothing about direction.
faults.fix: 'Swapping the supply leads does not reverse it.'

faults.finding: A button that stands for pushing a live shaft round reads as a method, with the warning only in the ignores panel.
faults.fix: Call it 'Spin the rotor', and put 'Picture only: never spin a live motor by hand' in the words under the picture.

faults.finding: 'Wind the start winding like the main' is an instruction; a read-through has no controls.
faults.fix: Say what each setting shows: 'With the start winding wound like the main, ...'.

faults.finding: With the main winding open the start winding alone could carry a pushed rotor up to the switch speed; the hint said it could not run once pushed.
faults.fix: It might run up once pushed, but the switch then drops the start winding out and nothing is fed, so it cannot keep running.
Cut each to about 90: tighter rows; 'Listen' moves to the practice list only; short row labels on screen 6.

faults.finding: Ring, waves, phasors, three readouts and two bars at 340 px are not given an order on a phone.
faults.fix: State the phone order: ring; phasors and waves side by side in one small panel; readouts; the two bars in one row.
'Example: 4.5 Ω and 15 Ω read 3.46 Ω together.'

faults.finding: None: 'Wound like the main' puts both currents in step and the field only pulses, so the cause (currents out of step) is seen on and off, besides the switch faults.
None: screen 3 asks for the direction of the cause through the impedance triangle, with a reversed-direction slip; screen 7 needs the cause reasoned from a symptom the still does not show.

None: the pulsing field, the thin-wire cause, the 30° angle, the sine rule, the switch speeds, the torque range, the short-time rating, the faults and the tests each rest on a research quote. Contested points (the angle's size, starting current) are given as ranges or examples.
